questions.q: What does the Release Manager own, per this lesson?
options: The technical correctness of every Apex class in the release
Running the CAB meeting itself
The release calendar and overall accountability for whether a given release actually ships on schedule
Approving every individual change's business impact personally
questions.explain: The Release Manager owns the process and calendar -- coordinating across teams and owning schedule accountability -- rather than personally approving technical content, which belongs to other named roles.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish release management roles from CAB membership?
options: They are exactly the same set of people with two different titles
Only the Release Manager is allowed to sit on the CAB
CAB membership replaces the need for any release management roles

Release management roles run the ongoing pipeline machinery; CAB membership is about who's in the room for a specific category of approval decision, and includes some non-release-management representatives like business stakeholders
questions.explain: Not every release management role sits on the CAB, and the CAB includes stakeholders who aren't release management roles at all -- the two concepts overlap but are not identical.

questions.q: What problem does this lesson identify with the 'architect approves everything' anti-pattern?
options: It becomes a severe bottleneck and a single point of failure as volume grows, and substitutes one person's judgment for the deliberately distributed review the chapter describes
It has no real downside as long as the architect is competent
It is required by Salesforce licensing terms for all orgs
It only applies to orgs with fewer than five users
questions.explain: Funneling every decision through one person feels safe short-term but creates a bottleneck and single point of failure, weakening governance rather than strengthening it as the program scales.

questions.q: In a RACI matrix as described in this lesson, who is typically 'Accountable' for a release's overall outcome?
options: Every end user affected by the change
Often the Release Manager for the release as a whole, and the CAB for the approval decision
Nobody -- RACI matrices don't assign accountability
Only the original change requester, with no other role involved
questions.explain: The lesson describes the Release Manager as typically Accountable for the release overall, with the CAB Accountable for the approval decision specifically, distinct from who is Responsible for doing the work.

questions.q: What does the Environment Manager role own, per this lesson?
options: The operational health of the environment path -- sandbox type availability, refresh scheduling, and preventing environment issues from blocking a release
Writing the Apex code for every deployed change
Chairing the Change Advisory Board
Deciding the organization's overall business strategy
questions.explain: The Environment Manager keeps the environment path operationally healthy -- the right sandboxes existing and refreshed on schedule -- so environment issues don't become what blocks a release.
